messages:
ravi: Heads up — after the kernel-selector change rolled yesterday we're seeing a host CPU spike (~+18%) on p99 for small payloads. Repro on canary. Suspect host-side tokenization + gRPC small-write pattern is the culprit.

sophia: Which commit/hash? @ravi can you paste the top flame or a perf snippet? :eyes:

ravi: Commit: 2026-03-20T02:14:22Z kernel-selector: prefer-fused-kernel-for-seq<32 (hash abc1234). Quick flame (sampler 5s):
```
tokenize/parse........... 45%
grpc::writev (many small syscalls) 20%
kv_cache::lock_contend.. 10%
http2::frame_assemble....8%
other sys overhead........17%
```
This lines up with host doing more micro work after we shifted to the fused GPU kernel (less GPU time, more concurrent host preproc).

liam: That matches a pattern we saw earlier: fused kernels shrink GPU latency but increase parallel host decode work. Batching heuristics matter — if we don't amortize tokenization across a few requests, we pay on CPU. Did the batching policy change in the same roll?

casey: I dug into gRPC traces: lots of small writev calls (~80-120 writes/s per connection) with payloads ~120-230 bytes. Nagle not enabled on our internal sockets sometimes; we end up pushing tiny frames. Ingress proxy is not coalescing because frame boundary logic assumes larger seqs.

ravi: Minimal repro (pseudo):
```bash
# small request flood to canary endpoint
for i in {1..200}; do grpc_cli call svc Gen "{input:\"short\"}" & done
# Capture perf: sudo perf record -F 100 -g -p <pid> -o perf.data
```
Attached the perf.data snippet in ticket.

sophia: Also noticed kv cache hit-rate drops during these spikes — kv_hit rate goes from 98% to 86% for short sequences. Hypothesis: increased concurrency from fused kernel path causes more simultaneous KV lookups and steals hot-shard locks, so more misses under contention.

alex: Quick experiment: rolled kernel-selector back on a canary host -> host CPU returned to baseline and kv_hit recovered. So the fused kernel is correlated. Mitigation idea: add a guard in kernel-selector: if median_seq_len < 24 && reqs_per_sec > threshold -> prefer non-fused kernel, or apply a soft cap on concurrent decode tasks.

casey: On the ingress side I can try two things for the canary: 1) coalesce small writes to target >512B before calling writev 2) tweak minibatch heuristic to prefer tiny batching (up to 4) for short seq workloads so tokenization is amortized. I'll run A/B tomorrow and report.

liam: Also consider a KV backpressure token: when kv_lock_waits > X increase batching or stall acceptance briefly. Could be an effective short-term knob.

deploy-bot: Deploy initiated: canary/ingress-coalesce+batch-heuristic -> eng-runtime-canary-1 at 03:20 UTC by casey

ravi: Thanks everyone. I'll open an ops/perf ticket with traces, flame, and the rollback experiment notes. cc @sophia @casey. Plan: ingress coalesce + batching tweak canary; add kernel-selector guard if canary confirms this tradeoff. :thumbsup:
